authorFindings: Regulator: medicine registration, import permits, advertising licences for medical products, the controlled and semi-controlled lists and compounding-pharmacy GCP certificates now sit with the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), created by Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (in force 30 Sep 2023) to succeed MOHAP. Official translations name it differently ('UAE Drug Corporation' on the legislation portal, 'Emirates Pharmaceutical Corporation' in DHA's list, 'Emirates Medicines Corporation' on the EDE legislation page); use 'Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE)'. MOHAP letterhead appears on the circulars read up to October 2024 (the Mounjaro alert says 'registered in MOHAP'); 2025-2026 circulars and approvals come from the EDE, although DHA attributed the June 2025 Melanotan II circular to MOHAP while DoH attributed the same warning to the EDE.

Off-label prescribing is conditioned in statute: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 Art. 42(1) allows uses outside the leaflet, or a product never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, with no equivalent alternative and with the patient's approval (ae-fdl-38-2024).

Dubai and Abu Dhabi diverged on peptides within two days: DHA (29 Jul 2026) prohibits any peptide product not registered or licensed with the EDE and any research-use peptide outside approved trials; DoH (31 Jul 2026) runs a risk-tiered model with compounding through licensed pharmacies, EDE-overseen APIs, full traceability, consent covering regulatory status and prior approval of any advertising, and its August 2026 compounding standard treats peptides as emerging substances usable only if monographed, an approved-medicine component or on the DoH registry. Notes must name the emirate (ae-dha-cir-peptides-2026, ae-doh-cir-148-2026, ae-doh-compounding-std-2026).

Federal compounding: products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies need no marketing approval (Art. 5(2)), but compounded essential copies of EDE-approved products are barred unless no commercial product can deliver the benefit (Art. 95(4)); since semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy injection and tablets, Rybelsus) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are registered, this copy rule bears directly on compounded GLP-1s. This is an inference from the two articles: no EDE statement on compounded GLP-1s was found.

Growth hormone and anabolic steroids are 'semi-controlled' medicines, not scheduled narcotics: every registered somatropin brand is dispensed as SCD, as are injectable testosterone, nandrolone, stanozolol and mesterolone; oral tretinoin, isotretinoin and acitretin are SCD too. Public advertising of controlled and semi-controlled products is banned (ae-mohap-md-306-2023, ae-ede-register, ae-fdl-38-2024).
Hair-loss products: no oral minoxidil product is registered (all 17 minoxidil entries are topical), while a topical finasteride spray (Fincrezo 2.275 mg/ml) has been registered since March 2025.

Recent EDE approvals relevant to the course: oral Wegovy (announced 1 June 2026, second country worldwide), orforglipron as Foundayo (3 April 2026, second country worldwide, months after the EDE's December 2025 warning about falsified 'orforglipron'), and upadacitinib (Rinvoq) for non-segmental vitiligo (17 Aug 2026, first country worldwide) (ae-ede-news-oral-wegovy, ae-ede-news-orforglipron, ae-ede-news-rinvoq-vitiligo). Ritlecitinib (Litfulo 50 mg) is also in the register.

Skin-clinic enforcement: exosome and PDRN products, including 'skin boosters' used with microneedling or mesotherapy, are unauthorised (EDE Circular 40/2026, 11 Sep 2026); glutathione injections for skin whitening are unregistered and must not be used (MOHAP, Oct 2021); Melanotan II warnings from MOHAP/EDE (June 2025) and DoH (July 2025); counterfeit and stolen Ozempic/Mounjaro alerts from 2024 to 2026.

Selling from clinics: licensed professionals other than pharmacists may not sell any medical product, directly or indirectly, without Ministry or health-authority approval (Art. 42(5)); only pharmaceutical establishments may sell prescription-only medicines (Art. 40); in Abu Dhabi, prescription-only medicines may be sold online only against a verified prescription (Circular 152/2026).

Cosmetics run on three tracks: ordinary cosmetics (MoIAT conformity under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014, plus Dubai Municipality Montaji registration in Dubai), 'cosmetics with a medical effect' registered by the EDE as healthcare products, and medicines. The EDE classification letter settles borderline products; Abu Dhabi treats topical cosmetic peptides as low risk.

Advertising: every medical-product advertisement, social media included, needs an EDE licence tied to a valid marketing authorisation and the approved indications, so unregistered peptides cannot lawfully be advertised. Dubai also bans titles such as 'Anti-Aging Specialist' or 'Aesthetic Consultant' and absolute claims.

Publication caution: the DoH circulars read (10/2025, 112/2025, 48/2026, 69/2026, 148/2026, 152/2026) say they 'should not be used as content for media publication', and the EDE and MOHAP circulars (EDE 20/2025, 31/2026, 40/2026; MOHAP 9217/2024) say they 'should not be used for media publication'. The integrator may prefer to keep those quotes in this file only (the registry's --no-quote-hosts option works per host: www.doh.gov.ae; the EDE/MOHAP circulars are hosted on www.dha.gov.ae, which also hosts DHA standards without that restriction).

Advertising compounded products: the EDE advertising licence requires a valid marketing authorisation and excuses only products exempted by the Cabinet under Art. 5(3); compounded products are exempt from marketing approval under Art. 5(2) instead, so on the service page's wording they cannot obtain an advertising licence (an inference; no EDE statement on advertising compounded products was found).

authorFindings: GLP-1 compounding is lawful in Brazil but narrow and heavily policed: NT 200/2025 permits it only under specific API conditions, all GLP-1 prescriptions have been retained by pharmacies since 23 Jun 2025, and ANVISA's 2026 enforcement closed 8 of 26 compounding pharmacies and importers inspected (Jan–Apr) and is working jointly with the Federal Police.

Semaglutide went off-patent in Brazil on 20 Mar 2026; ANVISA registered the first synthetic semaglutide (Ozivy, 26 May 2026) and five more on 29 Jul 2026, so 15 semaglutide products were active on 25 Sep 2026. The synthetic copies are for type 2 diabetes only; weight-management labelling sits with Wegovy (and Mounjaro for tirzepatide).

ANVISA's 2 Jul 2026 statement names GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500, CJC-1295 and ipamorelin as not registered in any category and 'illegal for any health use, including aesthetic'; it also says only substances with efficacy and safety assessment may be compounded, which rules out compounding these peptides.

The CFM bans hormone use for anti-ageing, including growth hormone (Res. 1.999/2012), and androgens or anabolic steroids for aesthetic purposes, plus 'bioidentical'/'nano' hormone marketing (Res. 2.333/2023). ANVISA banned aesthetic hormonal implants ('chip da beleza') in Nov 2024. Both apply directly to aesthetic-hormone practice.

Somatropin is a List C5 anabolic (two-copy special-control prescription), and Law 9.965/2000 requires prescription retention with the ICD code for 'anabolic steroids or peptides'. Gestrinone, DHEA, somatrogon and somapacitan are also on C5.

Brazil-specific label differences: topical tretinoin (Vitacid) is labelled for cutaneous photoageing; Olumiant is labelled for severe alopecia areata from age 12; the Propecia brand is inactive but 1 mg finasteride products (e.g. Pro Hair) are registered; no active oral minoxidil registration exists (Loniten inactive).

Oral collagen: Brazil authorises a skin-health claim for 2 kDa bioactive collagen peptides in food supplements (ANVISA Q&A, 9th ed., 16 Jan 2025). This is a regulated supplement claim, not a medicine indication. Supplements are oral only by definition.

Retatrutide is unregistered everywhere; ANVISA ordered seizure of all retatrutide-based products from an unidentified manufacturer sold online (RE 3.480/2026, 3 Sep 2026), found it in irregular supply chains in 3 states, and said the developer has not applied for registration. ANVISA refused clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren (LUM-201) in Jun 2026.

Criminal exposure: dealing in unregistered medicines is a Penal Code art. 273 offence (1–3 years' imprisonment after STF Tema 1003). ANVISA fiscal measures apply to 'any natural or legal persons or media outlets' that sell or advertise the products.

Doctors' social media: CFM 2.336/2023 forbids promoting medicines not registered with ANVISA and regulates before-and-after images. RDC 96/2008 limits prescription-medicine promotion to prescribers and dispensers, and ANVISA treats public advertising of compounded products as prohibited.

ANVISA's consultation site (consultas.anvisa.gov.br) blocks plain HTTP clients with Cloudflare but works in a browser; the open-data register at dados.anvisa.gov.br is freely downloadable and was used for conclusive absence checks.

authorFindings: Directive 2001/83/EC is still the EU medicines code: EUR-Lex shows the 1 January 2025 consolidation as current with no end date. Its replacement (the 'Union code', procedure 2023/0132 (COD)) was politically agreed and, per Council note 12263/26 of 21 September 2026, awaits the Council's first-reading position and Parliament's second reading (eu-council-st-12263-2026). Re-check before publishing, and date every EU statement.

The EU has no counterpart to US 503A/503B compounding categories: magistral and officinal preparations sit outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3) and pharmacy preparation is exempt from manufacturing authorisation (Article 40(2)), so the rules on what a pharmacy may compound, and from which active substances, are national. Do not map FDA category lists onto EU learners.

The EU line for peptide skin products runs through three instruments: a topical product with a cosmetic purpose is a cosmetic (1223/2009); anything injected or implanted is never a cosmetic (Art 2(2)), nor is a vial product sold with an injecting device or a needle-roller product reaching the dermis (borderline manual); an injected product without a medical purpose may be a device (MDR Annex XVI fillers), and anything acting pharmacologically is a medicine (2001/83 Art 1(2), with Art 2(2) resolving doubt towards medicines law).

Several substances in the course are banned from EU cosmetics outright: tretinoin (Annex II/375), minoxidil (II/372), oestrogens (II/260), progestogens (II/194), substances with androgenic effect (II/37) and steroidal anti-androgens (II/390). A 'cosmeceutical' containing them is an illegal cosmetic, whatever its label says.

Collagen marketing: the EU refused a VeriSol®P collagen-peptide claim on skin elasticity and wrinkles (Regulation 1154/2014) and the general 'collagen helps skin firmness and elasticity' claim is non-authorised in the EU Register (POL-HC-8291). The only authorised claim that mentions skin collagen is the vitamin C claim, which explains why EU collagen supplements often add vitamin C.

Orphan designations are not authorisations but appear in marketing: ibutamoren mesilate (MK-677) holds EU/3/17/1882 for growth hormone deficiency (2017), and afamelanotide holds designations beyond EPP (e.g. xeroderma pigmentosum and variegate porphyria, 2024, per EMA's orphan-designation table read 25 September 2026).

EMA's medicines table (25 September 2026) also lists items the course may want: Litfulo (ritlecitinib), a second JAK inhibitor, centrally authorised on 15 September 2023 and indicated for severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over (EMA data table); long-acting growth hormones Sogroya (somapacitan, 2021), Ngenla (somatrogon, 2022) and Skytrofa (lonapegsomatropin, 2022); and Kayshild (semaglutide, 2026) for MASH. Verify indications from the EPARs before using them.

Safety updates EU clinicians should know: semaglutide — NAION very rare side effect (PRAC, June 2025); finasteride — suicidal ideation confirmed, patient card (2025); topical minoxidil — infant hypertrichosis warning (2024); JAK inhibitors — restricted use in higher-risk groups (2023); topical retinoids — not in pregnancy (2018).

The June 2024 EMA/HMA call not to use GLP-1 receptor agonists for cosmetic weight loss was issued during shortages; EMA's shortage table now marks the Ozempic shortage resolved (last updated 13 January 2026), but the statement that these medicines are not approved for cosmetic weight loss remains true of their authorised indications.

Europol's SHIELD VI summary (25 February 2026) describes a Spanish network supplying illegal medicines and health products for cosmetic medicine to legal and clandestine clinics, with activity extending to Portugal — useful context for the PT file.

Method note: EUR-Lex answers automated requests with an empty 202 (bot protection), so every EU legal text was read from the Publications Office (Cellar) copy of the same document; the source URLs point there so the claim-support fetcher can read them, and each note gives the EUR-Lex link for learners. CosIng, the EU claims register screen and Europol are JavaScript pages read in a browser.

authorFindings: Where Portugal adds to the EU note: baricitinib (Olumiant) and afamelanotide (Scenesse) are classified 'MSRM restrita – alínea a)', i.e. exclusive hospital use, so neither can be dispensed by a community pharmacy for alopecia areata or EPP; Scenesse is authorised but has no marketed presentation in Portugal. Somatropin is 'MSRM restrita – alínea b)', distributed free through hospital endocrinology/paediatric services under CNNHC conditions.

INFARMED's Circular 045/2024 (4 Jul 2024) told prescribers not to prescribe Ozempic, Trulicity or Victoza to non-diabetic patients; Wegovy and Mounjaro carry the weight-management indication and are prescription-only (MSRM, 0% reimbursement on the presentations viewed).

Compounding in Portugal is pharmacy-only magistral/officinal preparation under a pharmacist (DL 95/2004, Portaria 594/2004), limited to pharmacopoeial or compendial raw materials, with an INFARMED banned list that also bars systemic doses above authorised doses. There is no 503B-style outsourcing route. The prescriber shares responsibility for the formula's safety and efficacy.

Import and sourcing: INFARMED does not authorise personal import of medicines (Circular 148/CD, 2011); online sale is legal only via pharmacies/licensed outlets on INFARMED's list with the EU logo; clinics holding medicines on unlicensed premises commit an offence fined up to €180,000 (Estatuto Art 181(2)(o)). Unauthorised peptides cannot be advertised at all (Art 152(1)).

Clinic marketing sits under two regimes: medicine advertising (INFARMED, Estatuto Arts 150-164) and health-services advertising (Decreto-Lei 238/2015, enforced by ERS, which bans claims of guaranteed results), plus the Ordem dos Médicos code (Art 56).

A clinician may find surprising: Portugal's anti-doping law (Lei 81/2021, Art 57) makes unauthorised selling, importing or illicit holding of listed substances a crime for anyone (1-5 years), not only in sport; the Ordem dos Farmacêuticos says pharmacists should not perform aesthetic procedures; topical minoxidil is a non-prescription medicine and Minox 5's label includes alopecia areata; the only authorised single-agent topical tretinoin (Ketrel) is labelled for acne and keratinisation disorders, not photoageing.

Infomed's conditions of use forbid republishing its content without INFARMED's written authorisation and prescribe a citation form ('Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed consultada em extranet.infarmed.pt/INFOMED-fo/index.xhtml (acedida em 25/09/2026)'); learner notes should state status facts and cite, not reproduce, Infomed records.

Oral collagen was given status 'unknown' because the enum has no value for a notified food supplement: in Portugal supplements are notified to DGAV, not authorised, and DGAV says notification never means a product is authorised or compliant.

The EMA/HMA GLP-1 warning relayed by INFARMED (5 Sep 2025) and Pangea XVIII (Mar 2026, weight-loss products among main seizures, 7 criminal inquiries over anabolic substances) are the dated Portuguese enforcement signals; no Portugal-specific melanotan or peptide alert was found.

claims.text: In the UAE, the EDE succeeded the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) in regulating medical products, and the 2023 law let the Cabinet keep MOHAP exercising these powers until the EDE carried out all its operations (Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, Arts. 15-16).

claims.subject: unlicensed

claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Without prejudice to the applicable legislation concerning veterinary preparations, it is not permitted to import, distribute, possess, sell, display, re-market, use, or manufacture any Medical Product in the State for circulation therein, except after obtaining Marketing Approval of any type from the EDE."

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In the UAE, physicians may prescribe a medicine for uses not in its leaflet, or a medicine never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, when no equivalent alternative is available and with the patient's approval; compassionate use is excluded from this rule (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 42(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Physicians may not prescribe a Medical Product for new uses not specified in the internal leaflet or electronic leaflet, or prescribe a Medical Product that has not been submitted for Marketing Approval, except when necessary, provided that there is no equivalent alternative available and with the patient approval. The compassionate use of the Medical Product is excluded from the provisions of this Clause."

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In the UAE, only pharmaceutical establishments may import, market, sell, display or store prescription-only medicines (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 40).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Non-Pharmaceutical Establishments are prohibited from importing, marketing, selling, displaying, storing or circulation any Medical Product that requires a prescription for dispensing."

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Dubai, the DHA prohibits circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE and used within the scope of its licence, and requires registered peptide products to be used strictly within their approved indications (External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In the UAE, medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from the marketing-approval requirement (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 5(2), in force 2 Jan 2025).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "As an exception to Clause (1) of this Article, all categories of Medical Products that are compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from the requirement to obtain Marketing Approval."

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In the UAE, a compounding pharmacy may not compound essential copies of products holding an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient, and may not formulate products intended for research, development or experimentation (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 95).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "The Compound Pharmacy is prohibited from the following: … 4. Commencing the installation of Medical Products that are essentially copies of Medical Products that have a valid Marketing Approval from the EDE, unless there is no commercially available Medical Product that can achieve the expected direct benefit to the patient health, and similar results could not be obtained by other means. 5. Compounding Pharmacies may not conduct any activities related to improvised, unstudied formulations or the extraction process of medicines and preparations derived from natural sources, and it is not permitted to formulate a Medical Product prepared for research, development or experimentation."

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH Standard for Provision of Compounding Pharmacy Services (August 2026) allows compounding only for a genuine, documented clinical need that no suitable licensed product meets, and bars copying commercially available products for convenience or cost or introducing experimental or unverified products.

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Abu Dhabi, compounding requires a Good Compounding Practice (GCP) certificate issued by the EDE, and compounding from unapproved or unknown-source substances, or from substances not on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances, is prohibited unless the DoH permits it (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).

claims.text: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH treats peptides as emerging, non-monographed, high-risk substances: novel substances of unknown risk may be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine, or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).

claims.text: In Abu Dhabi, compounded peptide formulations may use only certified active ingredients imported under EDE oversight, clinics must hold technical agreements with licensed compounding pharmacies, and peptide products must be traceable from source to patient (DoH Circular 148/2026, 31 July 2026).

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In the UAE, importing any medical product, or the raw materials used to make it, requires an EDE approval or permit (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 31).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "It is not permitted to import, export or re-export any Medical Product or any raw materials or pharmaceutical raw materials used in its manufacture except after obtaining approval or permit from the EDE."

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In the UAE, the conditions for bringing a medicine in for personal use, carried by a traveller or sent by express courier, are set by executive regulation (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 35); the 2021 executive regulation sets them in its Annex 1 (Cabinet Resolution 90/2021, Art. 4).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "The Executive Regulations of this Decree-Law shall specify the conditions, rules and controls for bringing, possessing or obtaining a Medical Product with any person upon entering or leaving the State for personal use, or bringing or sending the Medical Product through express shipping institutions."

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In the UAE, the EDE lets travellers bring medicines that are not narcotic or psychotropic without prior submission; narcotic and psychotropic (controlled) medicines may be carried within three months' need with a prescription or medical report, and residents can obtain EDE approval to import such medicines for personal use through shipping companies (EDE personal-import service, read 25 Sep 2026).

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Dubai, facilities may not buy, accept or use peptide products from websites, social media, individual accounts or unlicensed or unverifiable suppliers, and products without full identification data (active substance, concentration, batch, expiry) may not be used (DHA External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).

claims.text: In Abu Dhabi, prescription-only medicines may not be sold or dispensed through websites or delivery apps unless a valid prescription from a licensed practitioner has been verified, and online delivery needs prior DoH approval (Circular 152/2026, 5 Aug 2026).

claims.text: In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 brings cosmetics with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails within its definition of medical products regulated by the EDE.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Cosmetics: Products with a medical effect that are used on the human body to produce a desired local effect on the skin, hair or nails and do not require a prescription or direct medical supervision for their sale when used."

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In the UAE, the EDE registers 'healthcare products' not intended to diagnose, treat or prevent disease, including dietary supplements, herbal products and cosmetics with a medical effect, through a marketing authorisation valid for five years (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).

claims.text: In the UAE, whether a borderline product (for example a peptide serum) needs an EDE marketing authorisation, and in which category, is settled by an EDE classification letter based on the product's presentation, composition, use and design (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).

claims.text: In the UAE, food supplements are medical products under Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, defined as oral products that support the diet and do not treat, diagnose or prevent disease.

claims.text: In the UAE, a company registering a healthcare product such as a supplement with the EDE must declare it free of hormones, steroids, antibiotics, heavy metals and pig derivatives (EDE healthcare-product requirements, read 25 Sep 2026).

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In the UAE, advertising or promoting any medical product by any means, including social media, requires EDE approval, and advertising controlled or semi-controlled products to the public is prohibited (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 44).

It is prohibited to advertise, publicize or promote Medical Products by any means, whether visual, written, audible or on social media, unless approved by the EDE. 2. Advertising, publicity or promotion to the public of controlled, semi-controlled, hazardous or toxic chemical precursors, products or substances, whether for human or veterinary use, is prohibited."

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In the UAE, an EDE licence to advertise a medical product requires a valid EDE marketing authorisation for the product (only products exempted by the Cabinet under Art. 5(3) of Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 are excused), a licensed pharmaceutical or healthcare establishment as applicant, and truthful, evidence-based content matching the approved indications (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).

claims.text: In the UAE, the federal health-advertisement regulation (Cabinet Resolution 7/2007) bars anyone from advertising or promoting products presented as related to a medical product without prior authorisation, and bans terms such as 'the only', 'unique' and 'best product'.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "No natural or legal person may advertise or promote the sale of products related to or that are likely to make anyone believe that such an advertisement or promotion is related to any medical product without prior authorization from the Ministry of Health. … Using words like 'the only', 'unique', 'best product', 'Beware of imitation!', 'Don't miss!' must be avoided."

claims.text: In Dubai, the DHA bans misleading or unproven peptide claims, including anti-aging, cell regeneration, weight loss, muscle building and improved appearance, unless the use is within the product's approved status, and requires any promotion of unregistered materials, including through influencers or social media, to stop (29 July 2026).

claims.subject: minoxidil
claims.text: In Brazil, minoxidil is registered as an anti-alopecia medicine (for example Aloxidil 5%, indicated for androgenetic alopecia in adult men); every active minoxidil registration sits in the anti-alopecia class, and the oral antihypertensive Loniten registrations are all inactive (register, 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Aloxidil® 5% (minoxidil) é indicado no tratamento da alopecia androgênica (calvície hereditária) em homens adultos." (English: "Aloxidil® 5% (minoxidil) is indicated for the treatment of androgenetic alopecia (hereditary baldness) in adult men.")

claims.subject: finasteride
claims.text: In Brazil, 1 mg finasteride products such as Pro Hair are registered for male-pattern hair loss in men and are not indicated for women or children; the Propecia brand registration is inactive (register, 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "PRO HAIR é indicado para o tratamento de homens com calvície de padrão masculino (alopecia androgênica), para aumentar o crescimento e prevenir a queda adicional de cabelo." (English: "PRO HAIR is indicated for the treatment of men with male-pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia), to increase growth and prevent further hair loss.")

claims.subject: somatropin
claims.text: In Brazil, somatropin is registered (for example Genotropin, Pfizer, registered 12 Aug 2019) for growth disorders in children and for replacement therapy in adults with severe growth hormone deficiency; skin or anti-ageing uses are not labelled indications.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Genotropin® também é indicado na terapia de reposição em adultos com deficiência de hormônio de crescimento acentuada." (English: "Genotropin® is also indicated for replacement therapy in adults with marked growth hormone deficiency.")

claims.subject: somatropin
claims.text: In Brazil, somatropin is a controlled substance on List C5 (anabolic substances) of Portaria SVS/MS 344/1998, as updated by RDC 1.036/2026, and needs a special-control prescription in two copies.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "LISTA - C5 LISTA DAS SUBSTÂNCIAS ANABOLIZANTES (Sujeitas à Receita de Controle Especial em duas vias) … 29. Somatropina (hormônio do crescimento humano)" (English: "LIST C5 – LIST OF ANABOLIC SUBSTANCES (subject to a special-control prescription in two copies) … 29. Somatropin (human growth hormone)")

claims.subject: tesamorelin
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin (including Egrifta) was found in ANVISA's register or online search (25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão disponíveis todos os dados de produtos (medicamentos) registrados no Brasil cadastrados no DATAVISA." (English: "All data on products (medicines) registered in Brazil that are recorded in DATAVISA are available.")

claims.subject: sermorelin
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register or online search (25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão disponíveis todos os dados de produtos (medicamentos) registrados no Brasil cadastrados no DATAVISA." (English: "All data on products (medicines) registered in Brazil that are recorded in DATAVISA are available.")

claims.subject: ipamorelin
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that injectable ipamorelin products are not registered in any category.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os produtos que se apresentam como peptídeos denominados GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 e Ipamorelina, que prometem efeitos estéticos ou melhora em quadros de saúde, também NÃO se encontram registrados na Anvisa." (English: "Products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin, which promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions, are also NOT registered with Anvisa.")

claims.subject: CJC-1295
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that CJC-1295 products are not registered in any category.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os produtos que se apresentam como peptídeos denominados GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 e Ipamorelina, que prometem efeitos estéticos ou melhora em quadros de saúde, também NÃO se encontram registrados na Anvisa." (English: "Products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin, which promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions, are also NOT registered with Anvisa.")

claims.subject: ibutamoren (MK-677)
claims.text: In Brazil, ibutamoren is not a registered medicine, and on 9 Jun 2026 ANVISA refused the clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren mesylate (LUM-201) (RE 2.318/2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 1º Indeferir petições relacionadas à Coordenação de Pesquisa Clínica em Medicamentos e Produtos Biológicos, conforme anexo. … Mesilato de ibutamoren (LUM-201)" (English: "Art. 1 To refuse petitions related to the Clinical Research Coordination for Medicines and Biological Products, as annexed. … Ibutamoren mesylate (LUM-201)")

claims.subject: BPC-157
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that BPC-157 is not registered as a medicine and is not authorised as a food supplement, and that no company has applied for supplement authorisation.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "No Brasil, substâncias como BPC-157 e TB-500 não possuem autorização de uso como suplemento alimentar e, até o momento, não há solicitações de empresas ou estudos submetidos à Anvisa para a regularização dessas substâncias como suplementos alimentares ." (English: "In Brazil, substances such as BPC-157 and TB-500 are not authorised for use as food supplements and, so far, no company applications or studies have been submitted to Anvisa to regularise these substances as food supplements.")

claims.subject: TB-500 (thymosin beta-4 fragment)
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that TB-500 is not registered as a medicine and is not authorised as a food supplement.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os produtos que se apresentam como peptídeos denominados GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 e Ipamorelina, que prometem efeitos estéticos ou melhora em quadros de saúde, também NÃO se encontram registrados na Anvisa." (English: "Products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin, which promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions, are also NOT registered with Anvisa.")

claims.subject: KPV
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing KPV was found in ANVISA's register (25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão disponíveis todos os dados de produtos (medicamentos) registrados no Brasil cadastrados no DATAVISA." (English: "All data on products (medicines) registered in Brazil that are recorded in DATAVISA are available.")

claims.subject: GHK-Cu
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that injectable GHK-Cu products are not registered and are illegal for any health or aesthetic use; topical GHK-Cu cosmetics are a separate category (see cosmetics).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os produtos que se apresentam como peptídeos denominados GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 e Ipamorelina, que prometem efeitos estéticos ou melhora em quadros de saúde, também NÃO se encontram registrados na Anvisa." (English: "Products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, TB500, CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin, which promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions, are also NOT registered with Anvisa.")

claims.subject: LL-37
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing LL-37 (cathelicidin) was found in ANVISA's register, and the substance is absent from ANVISA's substance dictionary (25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão disponíveis todos os dados de produtos (medicamentos) registrados no Brasil cadastrados no DATAVISA." (English: "All data on products (medicines) registered in Brazil that are recorded in DATAVISA are available.")

claims.subject: thymulin
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing thymulin was found in ANVISA's register (25 Sep 2026); thymus-derived immunomodulators with other actives (thymomodulin, Leucogen; thymostimulin) do hold active registrations.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: ""MEDICAMENTO";"LEUCOGEN";"19/11/2003";"Específico";105730062;"022028";"2500100242582";"IMUNOMODULADOR";"60659463002992 - ACHÉ LABORATÓRIOS FARMACÊUTICOS S.A";"Ativo";"timomodulina"" (English: "Register row: medicine LEUCOGEN, specific-medicine category, registration 105730062, class immunomodulator, Aché Laboratórios, status Active, active substance thymomodulin.")

claims.subject: PTD-DBM
claims.text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing PTD-DBM was found in ANVISA's register (25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão disponíveis todos os dados de produtos (medicamentos) registrados no Brasil cadastrados no DATAVISA." (English: "All data on products (medicines) registered in Brazil that are recorded in DATAVISA are available.")

claims.subject: topical tretinoin
claims.text: In Brazil, topical tretinoin (for example Vitacid, Theraskin) is registered, and its label names cutaneous photoageing as well as acne vulgaris, for dermatological use in adults and patients over 12.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Vitacid® é indicado para o tratamento fotoenvelhecimento cutâneo, proporcionando a melhora de alguns sinais associados a essa condição. É indicado também no tratamento da acne vulgar, em que predominam comedões, pápulas e pústulas." (English: "Vitacid® is indicated for the treatment of cutaneous photoageing, improving some signs associated with this condition. It is also indicated for the treatment of acne vulgaris in which comedones, papules and pustules predominate.")

claims.subject: estradiol (menopausal hormone therapy)
claims.text: In Brazil, estradiol for menopausal hormone therapy is registered (for example Oestrogel, Besins); the label read covers menopausal symptoms and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis, and skin ageing is not a labelled indication.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Oestrogel® é indicado para o tratamento de sinais e sintomas oriundos da deficiência estrogênica relacionados à menopausa natural ou cirúrgica (fogachos, atrofia urogenital, distúrbio no sono e astenia) e prevenção da osteoporose (perda óssea) pós-menopausa." (English: "Oestrogel® is indicated for the treatment of signs and symptoms of oestrogen deficiency related to natural or surgical menopause (hot flushes, urogenital atrophy, sleep disturbance and asthenia) and for prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis (bone loss).")

claims.subject: oral collagen
claims.text: In Brazil, oral collagen is regulated as a food supplement, not a medicine; ANVISA's Jan 2025 guidance lists an approved skin-health claim for 2 kDa bioactive collagen peptides, restricted to products meeting an ANVISA-set minimum content, for adults only.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "“Os peptídeos bioativos de colágeno hidrolisado com peso molecular médio de 2 kDa auxiliam na manutenção da saúde da pele.”" (English: "“Bioactive hydrolysed collagen peptides with an average molecular weight of 2 kDa help maintain skin health.”")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Brazil, a compounded (magistral) preparation must be made individually by the pharmacy against a prescription from an authorised professional that sets its composition, form and dosing (RDC 96/2008 definition).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "PREPARAÇÃO MAGISTRAL - É aquela preparada na farmácia, de forma individualizada, para ser dispensada atendendo a uma prescrição de um profissional habilitado, respeitada a legislação vigente, que estabelece sua composição, forma farmacêutica, posologia e modo de usar." (English: "MAGISTRAL PREPARATION – One prepared in the pharmacy, individually, to be dispensed against a prescription from an authorised professional, in accordance with current legislation, which sets its composition, dosage form, dosing and directions for use.")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on a medical prescription, by a compounding pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Para ser manipulada, qualquer substância precisa ter passado por análises de eficácia e segurança. Além disso, a manipulação de qualquer fórmula SÓ pode ocorrer de forma individualizada, com apresentação de receita médica, por farmácias de manipulação que estejam devidamente regularizadas na vigilância sanitária local." (English: "To be compounded, any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessments. In addition, compounding of any formula may ONLY take place individually, on presentation of a medical prescription, by compounding pharmacies duly licensed by local health surveillance.")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Nov 2024 that compounded medicines should be used only when the registered industrial product is unavailable in the dose or dosage form the patient needs, and that only APIs with a current or past registration may be compounded into hormonal implants.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Anvisa ressalta que medicamentos manipulados devem ser utilizados somente diante da indisponibilidade do produto industrializado, registrado na Agência, na dosagem ou forma farmacêutica específica necessária ao paciente, e a partir de avaliação e da prescrição do profissional médico responsável." (English: "Anvisa stresses that compounded medicines should be used only when the industrialised product registered with the Agency is unavailable in the specific dose or dosage form the patient needs, and following assessment and prescription by the responsible physician.")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Brazil, Nota Técnica 200/2025 (Aug 2025) allows compounding of GLP-1 agonists only in narrow conditions: synthetic APIs only if a registered medicine with the same molecule exists, biotech APIs only from the manufacturer assessed at registration, with mandatory quality testing; at that date synthetic semaglutide could not be imported or compounded.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "No caso dos IFAs obtidos por síntese química, a manipulação é permitida desde que já existam medicamentos registrados no Brasil com a mesma molécula. … Por exemplo, atualmente, a semaglutida possui registro apenas como produto biotecnológico. Portanto, não é permitida a importação nem a manipulação da semaglutida sintética até que exista um medicamento registrado com o IFA sintético." (English: "For APIs obtained by chemical synthesis, compounding is permitted provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil. … For example, semaglutide is currently registered only as a biotechnological product. Therefore, import and compounding of synthetic semaglutide are not permitted until a medicine with the synthetic API is registered.")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA announced on 6 Apr 2026 an action plan to revise the compounding good-practice rule (RDC 67/2007) and Nota Técnica 200/2025 for GLP-1 pens, and scheduled a draft normative instruction on GLP-1/GIP compounding for Collegiate Board discussion on 29 Apr 2026.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "São parte do novo plano de ação da Anvisa as revisões das regras atuais para manipulação desses medicamentos, que incluem a Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada (RDC) 67/2007 e a Nota Técnica 200/2025 ." (English: "Part of Anvisa's new action plan is the revision of the current rules for compounding these medicines, which include Collegiate Board Resolution (RDC) 67/2007 and Technical Note 200/2025.")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Apr 2025 that its measure does not change the physician's right to prescribe medicines for purposes other than those on the label (off-label use), when the physician considers that, for a given patient, the benefits outweigh the risks.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A medida não altera o direito do profissional médico de prescrever medicamentos para finalidades diferentes das descritas na bula. Essa prática, conhecida como uso "off label", acontece quando o médico entende que, para determinado paciente, os benefícios do tratamento superam os riscos." (English: "The measure does not change the physician's right to prescribe medicines for purposes other than those described in the label. This practice, known as "off-label" use, occurs when the physician considers that, for a given patient, the benefits of treatment outweigh the risks.")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Brazil, no medicine, including an imported one, may be manufactured, sold or supplied before it is registered (Law 6.360/1976, art. 12).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 12 - Nenhum dos produtos de que trata esta Lei, inclusive os importados, poderá ser industrializado, exposto à venda ou entregue ao consumo antes de registrado no Ministério da Saúde." (English: "Art. 12 – None of the products covered by this Law, including imported ones, may be manufactured, offered for sale or supplied for consumption before being registered with the Ministry of Health.")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or supplement) and are therefore illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Não à toa, alguns peptídeos injetáveis NÃO estão regularizados na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) em nenhuma categoria - alimento, medicamento, cosmético, suplemento alimentar -, ou seja, são ILEGAIS para qualquer uso em saúde, inclusive estético." (English: "Not surprisingly, some injectable peptides are NOT regularised with the National Health Surveillance Agency (Anvisa) in any category – food, medicine, cosmetic, food supplement – that is, they are ILLEGAL for any health use, including aesthetic use.")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Jul 2026 that an investigational (experimental) medicine is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "O medicamento experimental, também chamado de medicamento investigacional, é utilizado exclusivamente em pesquisas clínicas autorizadas." (English: "An experimental medicine, also called an investigational medicine, is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.")

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Brazil, personal import of medicines for one's own use does not need prior ANVISA authorisation (RDC 81/2008 chapter XII, as amended by RDC 28/2011), but quantities must be for personal use and ANVISA may ask for the prescription.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A importação por pessoa física de bens ou de produtos sujeitos ao controle sanitário é regulamentada pelo Capítulo XII da Resolução de Diretoria Colegiada (RDC) 81, de 5 de novembro de 2008 , com as alterações promovidas pela RDC 28, de 28 de junho de 2011." (English: "Import by individuals of goods or products subject to health control is regulated by Chapter XII of Collegiate Board Resolution (RDC) 81 of 5 November 2008, as amended by RDC 28 of 28 June 2011.")

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Brazil, unregistered medicines may be imported only exceptionally, for strictly personal use, with a medical prescription; when ANVISA publishes a specific prohibition (as for several GLP-1 pens in 2025–2026), import by any route is suspended.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Medicamentos sem registro no Brasil só podem ser importados de forma excepcional e para uso exclusivamente pessoal, mediante prescrição médica e o cumprimento de requisitos adicionais. Porém, nos casos em que a Anvisa publica proibição específica, a importação, por qualquer modalidade, também fica suspensa." (English: "Medicines without registration in Brazil may only be imported exceptionally and for exclusively personal use, on medical prescription and subject to additional requirements. However, where Anvisa publishes a specific prohibition, import by any route is also suspended.")

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Sep 2025 that use of an unregistered imported medicine is entirely the responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Outro alerta: medicamentos sem registro no Brasil não tiveram sua segurança e eficácia avaliadas pela Agência. Seu uso é de inteira responsabilidade do paciente e do médico prescritor, além do risco de falsificação no mercado internacional." (English: "Another warning: medicines without registration in Brazil have not had their safety and efficacy assessed by the Agency. Their use is the entire responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician, besides the risk of falsification on the international market.")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Brazil, cosmetics are defined as preparations for external use on the body to clean, perfume, change appearance, correct odours or protect and keep it in good condition (RDC 907/2024, which revoked RDC 752/2022 in Sep 2024).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "XVI - produtos de higiene pessoal, cosméticos e perfumes: são preparações constituídas por substâncias naturais ou sintéticas, de uso externo nas diversas partes do corpo humano, pele, sistema capilar, unhas, lábios, órgãos genitais externos, dentes e membranas mucosas da cavidade oral, com o objetivo exclusivo ou principal de limpá- los, perfumá-los, alterar sua aparência e ou corrigir odores corporais e ou protegê-los ou mantê-los em bom estado;" (English: "XVI – personal hygiene products, cosmetics and perfumes: preparations made of natural or synthetic substances for external use on the various parts of the human body, skin, hair, nails, lips, external genitalia, teeth and oral mucosa, with the exclusive or main aim of cleaning them, perfuming them, changing their appearance and/or correcting body odours and/or protecting them or keeping them in good condition;")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Brazil, cosmetic labelling may not carry therapeutic claims for the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12), so a peptide serum that claims to treat a condition falls outside the cosmetic category.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 12. A rotulagem não deve conter nome comercial, marcas, imagens, links eletrônicos ou dizeres que: … II - representem alegações terapêuticas atribuídas ao uso do produto ou de seus ingredientes" (English: "Art. 12. Labelling must not contain trade names, brands, images, electronic links or wording that: … II – represent therapeutic claims attributed to the use of the product or its ingredients")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist; an injectable product offered as a cosmetic is irregular. Topical products named after GHK-Cu do appear as notified cosmetics in ANVISA's cosmetics dataset (221 entries, 25 Sep 2026); ANVISA cancelled several GHK-Cu cosmetic processes on 29 Apr 2026 without published reasons (RE 1.771/2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Por fim, apesar de suposta finalidade estética, esses produtos também NÃO são cosméticos. Não existem cosméticos injetáveis e, se o produto é oferecido desta forma, trata-se de cosmético irregular." (English: "Finally, despite their supposed aesthetic purpose, these products are also NOT cosmetics. Injectable cosmetics do not exist and, if the product is offered in this form, it is an irregular cosmetic.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Brazil, a food supplement is by definition a product for oral ingestion for healthy people (RDC 243/2018), so no injectable supplement can exist.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "VII - suplemento alimentar: produto para ingestão oral, apresentado em formas farmacêuticas, destinado a suplementar a alimentação de indivíduos saudáveis com nutrientes, substâncias bioativas, enzimas ou probióticos, isolados ou combinados." (English: "VII – food supplement: a product for oral ingestion, presented in pharmaceutical forms, intended to supplement the diet of healthy individuals with nutrients, bioactive substances, enzymes or probiotics, alone or combined.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Brazil, the constituents a food supplement may use are those on ANVISA's authorised list (IN 28/2018); constituents not on the list must not be used.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os constituintes autorizados constam da lista aprovada na IN 28/2018 e são diferentes para os seguintes grupos etários: 0 a 3 anos (Anexo II) e acima de 3 anos (Anexo I). … Constituintes que não constem dessa lista não devem ser utilizados." (English: "Authorised constituents are on the list approved in IN 28/2018 and differ for the following age groups: 0 to 3 years (Annex II) and over 3 years (Annex I). … Constituents not on this list must not be used.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Brazil, collagen is authorised in supplements both as a protein source and as three bioactive forms, and ANVISA lists an approved skin-health claim for 2 kDa bioactive collagen peptides (guidance of 16 Jan 2025); these products must carry a warning against use in pregnancy, lactation and children.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "No entanto, a atualização do marco normativo permitiu que o colágeno também fosse autorizado em suplementos alimentares como substância bioativa." (English: "However, the update of the regulatory framework allowed collagen also to be authorised in food supplements as a bioactive substance.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Brazil, federal law limits advertising of medicines and therapies to specialised publications aimed at health professionals, while over-the-counter medicines may be advertised to the public with warnings (Law 9.294/1996, art. 7).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 7° A propaganda de medicamentos e terapias de qualquer tipo ou espécie poderá ser feita em publicações especializadas dirigidas direta e especificamente a profissionais e instituições de saúde." (English: "Art. 7 Advertising of medicines and therapies of any type or kind may be carried out in specialised publications addressed directly and specifically to health professionals and institutions.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Brazil, promotion of prescription-only medicines is restricted to media aimed exclusively at professionals who can prescribe or dispense them, and online promotion must sit behind a registration wall for those professionals (RDC 96/2008, arts 27 and 29).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 29 A propaganda ou publicidade de medicamentos de venda sob prescrição veiculada na internet deve ser acessível, exclusivamente, aos profissionais habilitados a prescrever ou dispensar medicamentos, por meio de sistema de cadastramento eletrônico" (English: "Art. 29 Advertising or publicity of prescription-only medicines on the internet must be accessible exclusively to professionals authorised to prescribe or dispense medicines, through an electronic registration system")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Brazil, compounding pharmacies may give only prescribers factual material naming active substances and referenced indications, with no brand names, prices or promotional content (RDC 96/2008, art. 36); ANVISA restated in Nov 2024 that advertising compounded products to the public is not permitted.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A norma também reforçou a proibição da propaganda de produtos manipulados para o público em geral, o que não é permitido na legislação atual." (English: "The rule also reinforced the prohibition on advertising compounded products to the general public, which is not permitted under current legislation.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA said in Nov 2025 that its bans on unregistered GLP-1 pens were prompted by irregular advertising and sale, including online, which is prohibited for medicines; on 27 Apr 2026 it suspended sale and advertising of products from several compounding pharmacies, including standardised compounded medicines sold online without individual prescriptions (REs 1.683 and 1.684/2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "As medidas foram motivadas pelo aumento das evidências de propaganda e comercialização irregulares das chamadas canetas emagrecedoras, inclusive na internet, o que é proibido para medicamentos no Brasil." (English: "The measures were prompted by growing evidence of irregular advertising and sale of so-called slimming pens, including on the internet, which is prohibited for medicines in Brazil.")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Brazil, dispensing of anabolic steroids or peptides requires the pharmacy to retain a carbon copy of a prescription from a registered physician or dentist that includes the ICD code (Law 9.965/2000).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 1 o A dispensação ou a venda de medicamentos do grupo terapêutico dos esteróides ou peptídeos anabolizantes para uso humano estarão restritas à apresentação e retenção, pela farmácia ou drogaria, da cópia carbonada de receita emitida por médico ou dentista devidamente registrados nos respectivos conselhos profissionais." (English: "Art. 1 Dispensing or sale of medicines of the therapeutic group of anabolic steroids or peptides for human use is restricted to presentation and retention, by the pharmacy or drugstore, of the carbon copy of a prescription issued by a physician or dentist duly registered with their professional councils.")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Brazil, List C5 (anabolic substances) of Portaria SVS/MS 344/1998, current version RDC 1.036/2026, includes somatropin, somatrogon, somapacitan, testosterone, DHEA and gestrinone; topical products with these substances need a prescription but no retention.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "2) os medicamentos de uso tópico contendo as substâncias desta Lista ficam sujeitos a VENDA SOB PRESCRIÇÃO MÉDICA SEM RETENÇÃO DE RECEITA." (English: "2) topical medicines containing the substances on this List are subject to SALE ON MEDICAL PRESCRIPTION WITHOUT PRESCRIPTION RETENTION.")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Brazil, since 23 Jun 2025 all GLP-1 agonist medicines (semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, tirzepatide and others), industrial or compounded, need a two-copy prescription valid 90 days that the pharmacy retains (RDC 973/2025 and IN 360/2025).

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Brazil, the Federal Council of Medicine bars physicians from using anabolic steroids or androgens for aesthetic purposes or performance, and from prescribing hormones marketed as "bioidentical" or "nano" without proof of superiority (CFM Resolution 2.333/2023, in force since its publication on 11 Apr 2023; listed as in force on 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 3º São vedados no exercício da Medicina, por serem destituídos de comprovação científica suficiente quanto ao seu benefício e segurança para o ser humano, o uso e a divulgação dos seguintes procedimentos: … II – Utilização de formulações de esteroides anabolizantes ou hormônios androgênicos com a finalidade estética; … IV – A prescrição de hormônios divulgados como “bioidênticos”, em formulação “nano” ou nomenclaturas de cunho comercial e sem a devida comprovação científica de superioridade clínica para a finalidade prevista nesta resolução." (English: "Art. 3 The following procedures are prohibited in medical practice, lacking sufficient scientific proof of benefit and safety for humans, as are their use and promotion: … II – Use of formulations of anabolic steroids or androgenic hormones for aesthetic purposes; … IV – The prescription of hormones promoted as “bioidentical”, in “nano” formulation or under commercial names, without due scientific proof of clinical superiority for the purpose set out in this resolution.")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Brazil, CFM Resolution 1.999/2012 (in force Sep 2026) bars physicians from using hormones, including growth hormone, to prevent, delay, modulate or reverse ageing, except to replace a diagnosed deficiency with proven benefit.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "III. Utilização de hormônios, em qualquer formulação, inclusive o hormônio de crescimento, exceto nas situações de deficiências diagnosticadas cuja reposição mostra evidências de benefícios cientificamente comprovados;" (English: "III. Use of hormones, in any formulation, including growth hormone, except in diagnosed deficiencies where replacement shows evidence of scientifically proven benefit;")

claims.text: In Brazil, CFM Resolution 2.336/2023 on medical advertising forbids physicians to promote medicines not registered with ANVISA or to take part in product advertising that implies guaranteed results; before-and-after images must show satisfactory and unsatisfactory outcomes and complications.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 11. É vedado ao médico e, naquilo que couber, às pessoas jurídicas, entes sindicais e associativos de natureza médica: … III– divulgar equipamento e/ou medicamento sem registro na Anvisa, ou agência que a suceda;" (English: "Art. 11. Physicians and, where applicable, medical legal entities, unions and associations are prohibited from: … III – promoting equipment and/or medicines not registered with Anvisa or its successor agency;")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA banned in Nov 2024 the compounding, sale and use of hormonal implants based on anabolic steroids or androgens for aesthetic, sporting or muscle-gain purposes ("chip da beleza"; RE 4.353/2024), and requires the ICD code on prescriptions, excluding purposes barred by CFM 2.333/2023.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Resolução 4.353/2024 atualizou as condições excepcionais para manipulação de implantes e proibiu a manipulação, a comercialização e o uso de implantes hormonais à base de esteroides anabolizantes ou hormônios androgênicos, para fins estéticos, esportivos ou de ganho de massa muscular." (English: "Resolution 4.353/2024 updated the exceptional conditions for compounding implants and banned the compounding, sale and use of hormonal implants based on anabolic steroids or androgenic hormones for aesthetic, sporting or muscle-gain purposes.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA ordered seizure of a falsified Ozempic lot (LP6F832) in Nov 2023 (RE 3.945/2023) and warned in Oct 2024 that Fiasp insulin pens were relabelled as Ozempic lot NP5K174.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Anvisa recebeu comunicado da empresa responsável pelo produto biológico Ozempic ® (semaglutida) – Novo Nordisk Farmacêutica do Brasil Ltda. – sobre a presença de unidades, no mercado brasileiro, do lote LP6F832 , válido até 11/2025." (English: "Anvisa received notice from the company responsible for the biological product Ozempic® (semaglutide) – Novo Nordisk Farmacêutica do Brasil Ltda. – of units of lot LP6F832, valid until 11/2025, on the Brazilian market.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA ordered seizure of a falsified Mounjaro lot (955010) on 14 Aug 2026 after Eli Lilly said it did not recognise the lot as original (RE 3.240/2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Motivação: Comunicado da empresa detentora do registro do medicamento ELI LILLY DO BRASIL LTDA, CNPJ 43.940.618/0001-44, informando que não reconhece como original o lote 955010 do medicamento MOUNJARO (tirzepatida), concluindo tratar-se de produto falsificado." (English: "Reason: Notice from the registration holder ELI LILLY DO BRASIL LTDA stating that it does not recognise lot 955010 of MOUNJARO (tirzepatide) as original, concluding that it is a falsified product.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA ordered seizure in Feb 2026 of unregistered pens including Lipoless, Tirzec, T.G. and all "Retatrutide 40mg" brands (RE 690/2026), and in Jun 2026 suspended all tirzepatide production at a compounding pharmacy selling standardised, non-individualised products without prescription (RE 2.238/2026).

As ações estão em desacordo com a definição de preparação magistral." (English: "The sale of a standardised, non-individualised compounded product without a proper medical prescription from a competent professional was proven. These actions do not comply with the definition of a magistral preparation.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA inspections between Jan and Apr 2026 led to interdiction of 8 of the 26 compounding pharmacies and importers assessed and seized over 1.3 million irregular injectable units; ANVISA and the Federal Police issued a joint technical note on 6 May 2026 on crimes involving irregular GLP-1 medicines.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Inspeções conduzidas pela Anvisa entre janeiro e abril resultaram na interdição de 8 dos 26 estabelecimentos avaliados, além da apreensão de mais de 1,3 milhão de unidades de medicamentos injetáveis irregulares e da adoção de mais de 11 medidas proibitivas envolvendo importação, comércio e uso desses produtos." (English: "Inspections by Anvisa between January and April led to the closure of 8 of the 26 establishments assessed, as well as the seizure of more than 1.3 million units of irregular injectable medicines and more than 11 prohibition measures on the import, trade and use of these products.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA issued a pharmacovigilance alert on 9 Feb 2026 on acute pancreatitis with GLP-1 agonists, stressing use only within labelled indications and linking misuse for weight loss without clinical need to higher risk.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Anvisa destaca que o uso indiscriminado e fora das indicações autorizadas, especialmente para emagrecimento sem necessidade clínica, eleva significativamente o risco de efeitos adversos e dificulta o diagnóstico precoce de complicações graves." (English: "Anvisa highlights that indiscriminate use outside authorised indications, especially for weight loss without clinical need, significantly raises the risk of adverse effects and hampers early diagnosis of serious complications.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Brazil, selling, storing for sale or distributing a medicine without the required registration is a crime under Penal Code art. 273 §1º-B(I); the Supreme Court (RE 979.962, Tema 1003; extended Jun 2023) held the 10–15-year penalty unconstitutional for these acts and restored 1–3 years' imprisonment plus fine.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "É inconstitucional a aplicação do preceito secundário do art. 273 do Código Penal, com redação dada pela Lei nº 9.677/98 (reclusão, de 10 a 15 anos, e multa), à hipótese prevista no seu § 1º-B, I, que versa sobre importar, vender, expor à venda, ter em depósito para vender ou, de qualquer forma, distribuir ou entregar produto sem registro no órgão de vigilância sanitária. Para estas situações específicas, fica repristinado o preceito secundário do art. 273, na sua redação originária (reclusão, de 1 a 3 anos, e multa)" (English: "Applying the penalty of art. 273 of the Penal Code as worded by Law 9.677/98 (10 to 15 years' imprisonment and a fine) to the case in its §1-B, I – importing, selling, offering for sale, holding in stock for sale or in any way distributing or supplying a product without registration with the health surveillance body – is unconstitutional. For these specific situations, the original penalty of art. 273 (1 to 3 years' imprisonment and a fine) is restored.")
