claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Só podem ser utilizadas na preparação de um medicamento manipulado matérias-primas inscritas na Farmacopeia Portuguesa, nas farmacopeias de outros Estados Partes na Convenção Relativa à Elaboração de Uma Farmacopeia Europeia, na Farmacopeia Europeia ou na documentação científica compendial … Não podem ser prescritos medicamentos manipulados que incluam matérias-primas diferentes das referidas no n.º 1" (English: "Only raw materials listed in the Portuguese Pharmacopoeia, the pharmacopoeias of other States Parties to the Convention on the Elaboration of a European Pharmacopoeia, the European Pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation may be used to prepare a compounded medicine … Compounded medicines containing raw materials other than those referred to in paragraph 1 may not be prescribed")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED's list of substances banned from compounding (Deliberação 1985/2015, in force since Nov 2015) bars animal-organ extracts, active substances at doses above those authorised for human medicines when the compounded medicine is for systemic use, a named list of anorectics and levothyroxine, and substances whose medicines were suspended or revoked for public-health reasons.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Na prescrição e na preparação de medicamentos manipulados não podem ser utilizados: a) Extratos de órgãos de animais; b) Substâncias ativas, em dosagens superiores às autorizadas para medicamentos de uso humano, quando o medicamento manipulado se destine a uso sistémico;" (English: "The following may not be used in the prescription and preparation of compounded medicines: a) extracts of animal organs; b) active substances at doses higher than those authorised for medicines for human use, when the compounded medicine is intended for systemic use;")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Portugal, magistral formulas and officinal preparations may be prepared only by the pharmacy's pharmacist technical director or under that pharmacist's supervision and control (Portaria 594/2004, good compounding practice).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A preparação de fórmulas magistrais ou de preparados oficinais só pode ser realizada pelo farmacêutico director técnico ou sob a sua supervisão e controlo;" (English: "Magistral formulas or officinal preparations may only be prepared by the pharmacist technical director or under their supervision and control;")

claims.subject: compounding
claims.text: In Portugal, breaches of the compounding rules are administrative offences fined from €2,000 up to €3,700 (individuals) or €44,700 (companies), with INFARMED as enforcer (Decreto-Lei 95/2004, Art 10).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A violação do disposto no n.º 1 do artigo 3.º e nos artigos 4.º a 8.º do presente diploma constitui contra-ordenação punível com coima no montante mínimo de € 2000 e máximo de € 3700 ou € 44700, consoante o agente seja pessoa singular ou colectiva." (English: "Breach of Article 3(1) and Articles 4 to 8 of this decree is an administrative offence punishable by a fine of at least €2,000 and at most €3,700 or €44,700, depending on whether the offender is an individual or a legal person.")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED may authorise exceptional use (AUE) of a medicine without a marketing authorisation, for example when it is clinically justified as indispensable and no authorised alternative exists (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 92).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "O INFARMED, I.P., pode autorizar a utilização em Portugal de medicamento não possuidor de qualquer das restantes autorizações previstas no presente decreto-lei … a) Mediante justificação clínica, sejam considerados imprescindíveis à prevenção, diagnóstico ou tratamento de determinadas patologias, desde que seja demonstrada a inexistência de alternativa no conjunto de medicamentos com autorização de introdução no mercado;" (English: "INFARMED may authorise the use in Portugal of a medicine holding none of the other authorisations provided for in this decree-law … a) where, on clinical justification, they are considered indispensable for preventing, diagnosing or treating certain conditions, provided it is shown that no alternative exists among medicines with a marketing authorisation;")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Portugal, a patient-specific AUE is granted to institutions authorised to buy medicines directly (e.g., hospitals) or used by community pharmacies under set conditions, and always requires an individual clinical justification that the medicine is indispensable (INFARMED Deliberação 840/2023, 31 Aug 2023).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A AUE destinada a doente específico pode ser concedida às entidades com autorização de aquisição direta de medicamentos … 3 — As autorizações previstas no presente artigo carecem de comprovação da imprescindibilidade do medicamento face às alternativas terapêuticas, mediante justificação clínica individualizada." (English: "A patient-specific AUE may be granted to entities authorised for direct purchase of medicines … 3 — The authorisations provided for in this article require proof that the medicine is indispensable compared with therapeutic alternatives, by means of an individualised clinical justification.")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED told prescribers in July 2024 that Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza should not be prescribed to people without diabetes, because off-label use (notably for weight loss) threatens supply for diabetic patients (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200, 4 Jul 2024).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os medicamentos Ozempic, Trulicity e Victoza não devem ser prescritos a doentes que não sejam diabéticos;" (English: "Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza must not be prescribed to patients who are not diabetic;")

claims.subject: unlicensed
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED stated in July 2024 that use of GLP-1 medicines outside their approved indications, notably for weight loss, had significantly worsened the shortage, and that reports of falsified GLP-1 medicines existed (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A utilização destes medicamentos para indicações que não se encontram aprovadas, nomeadamente na perda de peso, tem contribuído, de forma significativa para o agravamento da situação." (English: "The use of these medicines for indications that are not approved, notably weight loss, has contributed significantly to the worsening of the situation.")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Portugal, a medicine is any substance presented as treating or preventing disease or used to restore, correct or modify physiological functions by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action, so a 'research use only' label does not take such a product outside medicines law (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 3).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "«Medicamento», toda a substância ou associação de substâncias apresentada como possuindo propriedades curativas ou preventivas de doenças em seres humanos ou dos seus sintomas ou que possa ser utilizada ou administrada no ser humano com vista a estabelecer um diagnóstico médico ou, exercendo uma ação farmacológica, imunológica ou metabólica, a restaurar, corrigir ou modificar funções fisiológicas;" (English: "'Medicine': any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease in human beings or its symptoms, or which may be used in or administered to human beings with a view to making a medical diagnosis or to restoring, correcting or modifying physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action;")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Portugal, placing any medicine on the market requires authorisation by INFARMED's governing body, unless the law provides otherwise (e.g., EU central authorisation) (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 14(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Salvo disposição em contrário, a comercialização de medicamentos no território nacional está sujeita a autorização do órgão máximo do INFARMED." (English: "Unless otherwise provided, the marketing of medicines in national territory is subject to authorisation by INFARMED's governing body.")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Portugal, making, selling, supplying or administering medicines without the required authorisation, or falsified medicines, is an administrative offence fined from €2,000 up to 15% of turnover or €180,000, whichever is lower (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 181(2)(a)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Constitui contraordenação, punível com coima entre (euro) 2 000 e 15 % do volume de negócios do responsável ou (euro) 180 000, consoante o que for inferior: a) O fabrico, introdução no mercado, comercialização, distribuição, intermediação, importação, exportação, importação paralela, dispensa, fornecimento ou venda ao público, ou administração de medicamentos ou medicamentos experimentais, bem como de substâncias ativas ou excipientes, sem as autorizações, ou registos, exigidas ou que sejam medicamentos falsificados;" (English: "It is an administrative offence, punishable by a fine between €2,000 and 15% of the offender's turnover or €180,000, whichever is lower: a) the manufacture, placing on the market, marketing, distribution, brokering, import, export, parallel import, dispensing, supply or sale to the public, or administration of medicines or investigational medicines, or of active substances or excipients, without the required authorisations or registrations, or that are falsified medicines;")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Portugal, storing or holding medicines on premises without the appropriate INFARMED licence is itself an offence in the same fine band (up to €180,000) (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 181(2)(o)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "o) A armazenagem, detenção ou posse de medicamentos em instalações não possuidoras de licenciamento adequado emitido pelo INFARMED, I.P." (English: "o) the storage, holding or possession of medicines in premises without an appropriate licence issued by INFARMED.")

claims.subject: research-use-only
claims.text: In Portugal, pharmacies and institutions authorised to buy medicines directly may acquire them only from entities authorised by INFARMED (except patient-specific exceptional imports) (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 79(4)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Salvo o disposto na alínea c) do n.º 1 do artigo 92.º, as farmácias e as entidades autorizadas à aquisição direta de medicamentos apenas podem adquiri-los a entidades autorizadas pelo INFARMED, I.P." (English: "Except as provided in Article 92(1)(c), pharmacies and entities authorised for direct purchase of medicines may only acquire them from entities authorised by INFARMED.")

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED does not authorise the import of medicines for personal use (Circular 148/CD, 29 Jul 2011).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Assim, o Infarmed não autoriza a importação de medicamentos para uso pessoal." (English: "Therefore, Infarmed does not authorise the import of medicines for personal use.")

claims.subject: import
claims.text: In Portugal, medicines may be sold online only by pharmacies and licensed non-prescription outlets registered with INFARMED, and since 1 Jul 2015 their websites must carry the EU common logo linking to INFARMED's list; prescription medicines delivered at home still require a prescription (INFARMED, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "passou a ser obrigatório, a partir de 1 de julho de 2015, que as páginas na Internet de farmácias e locais de venda de medicamentos não sujeitos a receita médica (LVMNSRM) que ofereçam legalmente medicamentos para venda à distância a residentes noutros Estados Membros da União Europeia, possuam o logótipo comum" (English: "it became mandatory from 1 July 2015 for the websites of pharmacies and non-prescription medicine outlets (LVMNSRM) that lawfully offer medicines for distance sale to residents of other EU Member States to display the common logo")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED is the national competent authority for cosmetic products under the EU Cosmetics Regulation (Decreto-Lei 23/2025, in force 24 Mar 2025).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "O INFARMED — Autoridade Nacional do Medicamento e Produtos de Saúde, I. P. (INFARMED, I. P.), é a autoridade nacional competente para efeitos do n.º 1 do artigo 34.º do Regulamento (CE) n.º 1223/2009 e do presente decreto-lei." (English: "INFARMED — National Authority of Medicines and Health Products, I.P., is the national competent authority for the purposes of Article 34(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 and of this decree-law.")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Portugal, it is prohibited to make or place on the market as a cosmetic any product that does not fit the EU definition of a cosmetic product (Decreto-Lei 23/2025, Art 4).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "É proibido o fabrico, a colocação ou a disponibilização no mercado nacional como produto cosmético, qualquer produto que não se integra na definição a que se refere a alínea a) do n.º 1 do artigo 2.º do Regulamento (CE) n.º 1223/2009." (English: "The manufacture, placing or making available on the national market as a cosmetic product of any product that does not fall within the definition in Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 is prohibited.")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED states that products administered by ingestion, inhalation, injection or implantation are not cosmetics, so an injected 'peptide' cannot be sold as a cosmetic (INFARMED cosmetics FAQ, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Não são considerados cosméticos produtos cuja administração se faça por ingestão, inalação, injeção ou implantação no corpo." (English: "Products administered by ingestion, inhalation, injection or implantation into the body are not considered cosmetics.")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Portugal, borderline products (such as topical 'peptide' serums with medicinal-sounding claims) must be classified case by case by the Responsible Person, using the European Commission borderline manual; cosmetics need no prior authorisation but are subject to INFARMED market surveillance (INFARMED cosmetics FAQ).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os produtos fronteira devem ser avaliados caso a caso pela Pessoa Responsável, tendo em conta todas as suas características." (English: "Borderline products must be assessed case by case by the Responsible Person, taking all their characteristics into account.")

claims.subject: cosmetics
claims.text: In Portugal, commercial imports of cosmetics from outside the EU need a declaration of conformity issued by INFARMED to clear customs (INFARMED cosmetics FAQ, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A apresentação da declaração de conformidade, nas Alfândegas, é obrigatória para proceder em território nacional ao desalfandegamento de produtos cosméticos provenientes de países terceiros, com carácter comercial." (English: "Presenting the declaration of conformity at customs is mandatory to clear, in national territory, cosmetic products of a commercial nature coming from third countries.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Portugal, food supplements are intended to maintain the body's homeostasis, not to prevent, treat or cure disease (DGAV, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os suplementos alimentares destinam-se a manter a homeostasia do organismo e não à prevenção, tratamento ou cura de doenças." (English: "Food supplements are intended to maintain the body's homeostasis and not to prevent, treat or cure diseases.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Portugal, every food supplement must be notified to DGAV before it is placed on the national market, even if already sold in another EU Member State (DGAV, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os Suplementos Alimentares têm de ser notificados à DGAV , antes de serem colocados no mercado nacional, mesmo os que já se encontram comercializados noutro Estado-Membro da UE" (English: "Food supplements must be notified to DGAV before being placed on the national market, even those already marketed in another EU Member State")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Portugal, DGAV warns that notifying a supplement does not mean it is authorised or compliant; there is no pre-market evaluation and control is by later sampling (DGAV, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "em caso algum, o operador poderá concluir que o produto se encontra autorizado ou que se encontra conforme." (English: "in no case may the operator conclude that the product is authorised or compliant.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Portugal, supplement ingredients other than vitamins and minerals (for example peptides or amino acids) must satisfy the EU Novel Food Regulation, i.e. show significant EU food consumption before 15 May 1997 or be authorised as novel foods (DGAV, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "têm de cumprir os requisitos do Regulamento (UE) 2015/2283 relativo a novos alimentos , isto é, têm de comprovadamente deter histórico de consumo alimentar significativo na União Europeia antes de 15 de maio de 1997 ." (English: "must meet the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 on novel foods, that is, they must be shown to have a significant history of food consumption in the European Union before 15 May 1997.")

claims.subject: supplements
claims.text: In Portugal, health claims on foods, including supplements such as oral collagen, are allowed only if they appear in the EU register of authorised claims under Regulation 1924/2006, with their conditions of use (DGAV, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "As alegações de saúde são sujeitas a um procedimento de autorização e estão disponíveis no Registo de Alegações Nutricionais e de Saúde Autorizadas e Rejeitadas da Comissão Europeia." (English: "Health claims are subject to an authorisation procedure and are available in the European Commission's Register of authorised and rejected nutrition and health claims.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, advertising any medicine that lacks a valid authorisation for the national market, or that is used only under an exceptional-use authorisation (Arts 92-93), is prohibited (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 152(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "É proibida a publicidade de medicamentos que não sejam objecto de uma autorização ou registo válidos para o mercado nacional ou que tenham sido autorizados ao abrigo do artigo 92.º e 93.º" (English: "Advertising of medicines that do not hold a valid authorisation or registration for the national market, or that were authorised under Articles 92 and 93, is prohibited")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, advertising prescription-only medicines to the general public is prohibited; they may be advertised only in technical publications or media intended for and accessible only to health professionals (Estatuto do Medicamento, Arts 152(2) and 154(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "É proibida a publicidade junto do público em geral dos medicamentos: a) Sujeitos a receita médica; … Os medicamentos sujeitos a receita médica só podem ser anunciados ou publicitados em publicações técnicas ou suportes de informação destinados e acessíveis exclusivamente por médicos e outros profissionais de saúde." (English: "Advertising to the general public of the following medicines is prohibited: a) those subject to medical prescription; … Prescription-only medicines may only be announced or advertised in technical publications or information media intended for and accessible exclusively to physicians and other health professionals.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, public advertising of non-prescription medicines (such as topical minoxidil) may not suggest that a healthy person's normal state of health can be improved by the medicine, nor present it as a food or cosmetic (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 153(4)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "c) Sugira que o estado normal de saúde da pessoa pode ser melhorado através da utilização do medicamento; … g) Trate o medicamento como um produto alimentar, produto cosmético ou de higiene corporal ou qualquer outro produto de consumo;" (English: "c) suggests that the person's normal state of health can be improved by using the medicine; … g) treats the medicine as a food, cosmetic or personal-hygiene product or any other consumer product;")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, the advertiser, the advertising agency, anyone disseminating the advertising and the owner of the advertising medium are all liable for breaches of the medicine-advertising rules, which can also bring publication of the sanction and a suspension of the medicine's advertising for up to two years (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 182).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "São punidos como autores ou coautores das contraordenações previstas no presente decreto-lei, relativamente à violação dos deveres previstos no capítulo IX, o anunciante, a agência de publicidade ou qualquer outra entidade que exerça a atividade publicitária, ou a divulgação de publicidade, o titular do suporte publicitário ou o respetivo concessionário." (English: "The advertiser, the advertising agency or any other entity carrying out the advertising activity or disseminating the advertising, and the owner of the advertising medium or its concessionaire, are punished as perpetrators or co-perpetrators of the offences under this decree-law concerning breaches of the duties in Chapter IX.")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, advertising of health services by any provider, public or private (including clinics offering aesthetic treatments), is regulated by Decreto-Lei 238/2015, which bans false claims of guaranteed cure or results or of absence of side effects.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "São proibidas as práticas de publicidade em saúde que, por qualquer razão, induzam ou sejam suscetíveis de induzir em erro o utente quanto à decisão a adotar, designadamente: … c) Se refiram falsamente a demonstrações ou garantias de cura ou de resultados ou sem efeitos adversos ou secundários;" (English: "Health advertising practices that, for any reason, mislead or are liable to mislead the user as to the decision to take are prohibited, namely those that: … c) falsely refer to demonstrations or guarantees of cure or of results, or of absence of adverse or side effects;")

claims.subject: advertising
claims.text: In Portugal, the health regulator ERS (Entidade Reguladora da Saúde) enforces the health-advertising rules, with fines of €250–€3,740.98 for individuals and €1,000–€44,891.81 for companies, plus possible bans of up to two years (Decreto-Lei 238/2015, Art 8).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Cabe à Entidade Reguladora da Saúde a fiscalização e a instrução dos processos de contraordenação, competindo ao respetivo conselho de administração a aplicação das correspondentes coimas e sanções acessórias." (English: "The Health Regulatory Authority is responsible for supervision and for investigating the offence proceedings, and its board of directors applies the corresponding fines and ancillary sanctions.")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Portugal, every medicine intended for parenteral administration (injection) is prescription-only by law (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 114(1)(d)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Estão sujeitos a receita médica os medicamentos que preencham uma das seguintes condições: … d) Destinem-se a ser administrados por via parentérica." (English: "Medicines meeting one of the following conditions are subject to medical prescription: … d) they are intended for parenteral administration.")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Portugal, 'restricted prescription' medicines (MSRM restrita) are reserved to specialised settings: alínea a) means exclusive hospital use (e.g., Olumiant, Scenesse) and alínea b) means conditions diagnosed only in hospital or specialised settings (e.g., somatropin) (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 118).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "a) Destinarem-se a uso exclusivo hospitalar, devido às suas características farmacológicas, à sua novidade, ou por razões de saúde pública; b) Destinarem-se a patologias cujo diagnóstico seja efectuado apenas em meio hospitalar ou estabelecimentos diferenciados com meios de diagnóstico adequados," (English: "a) they are intended for exclusive hospital use because of their pharmacological characteristics, their novelty, or for public-health reasons; b) they are intended for conditions whose diagnosis is made only in hospital or in specialised establishments with appropriate diagnostic means,")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Portugal, growth hormone is distributed free of charge through hospitals with endocrinology or paediatric services, and a national commission (CNNHC) sets the conditions for its administration (INFARMED, read 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "À Comissão Nacional para a Normalização da Hormona do Crescimento compete a definição das condições de administração da hormona de crescimento, que é distribuída gratuitamente nas instituições hospitalares com serviços de endocrinologia e/ou serviços de pediatria," (English: "The National Commission for the Standardisation of Growth Hormone is responsible for defining the conditions of administration of growth hormone, which is distributed free of charge in hospital institutions with endocrinology and/or paediatric services,")

claims.subject: controlled
claims.text: In Portugal, anyone who without authorisation makes, sells, distributes, buys, receives, imports or illicitly holds substances on the anti-doping prohibited list commits a crime punishable by 1 to 5 years' imprisonment; the offence is not limited to athletes (Lei 81/2021, Art 57).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Quem, sem que para tal se encontre autorizado, produzir, fabricar, extrair, preparar, oferecer, puser à venda, vender, distribuir, comprar, ceder, ou por qualquer título receber, proporcionar a outrem, transportar, importar, exportar ou fizer transitar ou ilicitamente detiver substâncias e métodos constantes da lista de substâncias e métodos proibidos é punido com pena de prisão de 1 a 5 anos." (English: "Whoever, without being authorised to do so, produces, manufactures, extracts, prepares, offers, puts up for sale, sells, distributes, buys, transfers, or receives by any title, provides to another, transports, imports, exports, transits or unlawfully holds substances and methods on the list of prohibited substances and methods is punished with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years.")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Portugal, the Ordem dos Médicos approved a Competence in Aesthetic Medicine on 12 Dec 2023, a voluntary title with defined training (the experience-based route closed on 31 Dec 2025); the regulation sets training criteria and does not address hormone or peptide prescribing.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Na Assembleia de Representantes, dia 12 de Dezembro 2023, foi aprovado o Regulamento da Competência de Medicina Estética" (English: "At the Assembly of Representatives on 12 December 2023, the Regulation of the Competence in Aesthetic Medicine was approved")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Portugal, the Ordem dos Médicos code gives physicians freedom to choose diagnostic and therapeutic means but requires decisions dictated by science and conscience and bars unnecessary or superfluous treatment (Regulamento 707/2016, Art 7).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "O médico só deve tomar decisões ditadas pela ciência e pela sua consciência. 2 — O médico tem liberdade de escolha de meios de diagnóstico e terapêutica, devendo, porém, abster-se de prescrever desnecessariamente exames ou tratamentos onerosos ou de realizar atos médicos supérfluos." (English: "The physician must only take decisions dictated by science and by conscience. 2 — The physician is free to choose diagnostic and therapeutic means but must refrain from unnecessarily prescribing costly tests or treatments or performing superfluous medical acts.")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Portugal, physicians may not publicise information that could be taken as a guarantee of results or as misleading advertising, and must avoid creating false needs for consumption (Ordem dos Médicos code, Regulamento 707/2016, Art 56).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "É vedada aos médicos a divulgação de informação suscetível de ser considerada como garantia de resultados ou que possa ser considerada publicidade enganosa." (English: "Physicians are prohibited from disseminating information liable to be regarded as a guarantee of results or that may be regarded as misleading advertising.")

claims.subject: professional
claims.text: In Portugal, the Ordem dos Farmacêuticos stated in Oct 2022 that it recognises no aesthetic procedure as a pharmaceutical act and that pharmacists should not perform them; their injection competence does not cover the facial area (Ordem dos Farmacêuticos, 26 Oct 2022).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A OF esclarece que a Competência Farmacêutica em Administração de Vacinas e Medicamentos Injetáveis não habilita o farmacêutico para a administração de medicamentos injetáveis na zona facial e que não reconhece qualquer procedimento estético como ato farmacêutico, pelo que o farmacêutico não os deve realizar." (English: "The OF clarifies that the Pharmaceutical Competence in Administration of Vaccines and Injectable Medicines does not qualify pharmacists to administer injectable medicines in the facial area, and that it recognises no aesthetic procedure as a pharmaceutical act, so pharmacists should not perform them.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED announced in Jan 2025 a broad programme of audits and inspections across the whole antidiabetic-medicine chain (marketing-authorisation holders, distributors, pharmacies and the health system), prompted by 2024 GLP-1 use data (INFARMED press release, 21 Jan 2025).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Face à análise dos dados de utilização disponíveis no final do ano de 2024, o INFARMED desencadeou um processo alargado de auditorias e inspeções a todo o circuito do medicamento, desde o fabricante e titular de autorização de introdução no mercado, aos distribuidores, farmácias e sistema de saúde." (English: "Following analysis of the use data available at the end of 2024, INFARMED launched a broad process of audits and inspections of the whole medicine circuit, from the manufacturer and marketing-authorisation holder to distributors, pharmacies and the health system.")

claims.subject: enforcement
claims.text: In Portugal, INFARMED relayed on 5 Sep 2025 the EMA/HMA warning of a sharp rise in illegal online sales of products presented as GLP-1 agonists (semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide), promoted on social media and not authorised.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Nos últimos meses, verificou-se um aumento acentuado na comercialização ilegal de medicamentos apresentados como agonistas do recetor GLP-1 – como o semaglutido, o liraglutido e a tirzepatida – destinados à perda de peso e ao tratamento da diabetes." (English: "In recent months there has been a sharp increase in the illegal marketing of medicines presented as GLP-1 receptor agonists – such as semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide – intended for weight loss and the treatment of diabetes.")

authorFindings: AE: Regulator: medicine registration, import permits, advertising licences for medical products, the controlled and semi-controlled lists and compounding-pharmacy GCP certificates now sit with the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), created by Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (in force 30 Sep 2023) to succeed MOHAP. Official translations name it differently ('UAE Drug Corporation' on the legislation portal, 'Emirates Pharmaceutical Corporation' in DHA's list, 'Emirates Medicines Corporation' on the EDE legislation page); use 'Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE)'. MOHAP letterhead appears on the circulars read up to October 2024 (the Mounjaro alert says 'registered in MOHAP'); 2025-2026 circulars and approvals come from the EDE, although DHA attributed the June 2025 Melanotan II circular to MOHAP while DoH attributed the same warning to the EDE.

AE: Off-label prescribing is conditioned in statute: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 Art. 42(1) allows uses outside the leaflet, or a product never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, with no equivalent alternative and with the patient's approval (ae-fdl-38-2024).

AE: Dubai and Abu Dhabi diverged on peptides within two days: DHA (29 Jul 2026) prohibits any peptide product not registered or licensed with the EDE and any research-use peptide outside approved trials; DoH (31 Jul 2026) runs a risk-tiered model with compounding through licensed pharmacies, EDE-overseen APIs, full traceability, consent covering regulatory status and prior approval of any advertising, and its August 2026 compounding standard treats peptides as emerging substances usable only if monographed, an approved-medicine component or on the DoH registry. Notes must name the emirate (ae-dha-cir-peptides-2026, ae-doh-cir-148-2026, ae-doh-compounding-std-2026).

AE: Federal compounding: products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies need no marketing approval (Art. 5(2)), but compounded essential copies of EDE-approved products are barred unless no commercial product can deliver the benefit (Art. 95(4)); since semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy injection and tablets, Rybelsus) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are registered, this copy rule bears directly on compounded GLP-1s. This is an inference from the two articles: no EDE statement on compounded GLP-1s was found.

AE: Growth hormone and anabolic steroids are 'semi-controlled' medicines, not scheduled narcotics: every registered somatropin brand is dispensed as SCD, as are injectable testosterone, nandrolone, stanozolol and mesterolone; oral tretinoin, isotretinoin and acitretin are SCD too. Public advertising of controlled and semi-controlled products is banned (ae-mohap-md-306-2023, ae-ede-register, ae-fdl-38-2024).
AE: Hair-loss products: no oral minoxidil product is registered (all 17 minoxidil entries are topical), while a topical finasteride spray (Fincrezo 2.275 mg/ml) has been registered since March 2025.

AE: Recent EDE approvals relevant to the course: oral Wegovy (announced 1 June 2026, second country worldwide), orforglipron as Foundayo (3 April 2026, second country worldwide, months after the EDE's December 2025 warning about falsified 'orforglipron'), and upadacitinib (Rinvoq) for non-segmental vitiligo (17 Aug 2026, first country worldwide) (ae-ede-news-oral-wegovy, ae-ede-news-orforglipron, ae-ede-news-rinvoq-vitiligo). Ritlecitinib (Litfulo 50 mg) is also in the register.

AE: Skin-clinic enforcement: exosome and PDRN products, including 'skin boosters' used with microneedling or mesotherapy, are unauthorised (EDE Circular 40/2026, 11 Sep 2026); glutathione injections for skin whitening are unregistered and must not be used (MOHAP, Oct 2021); Melanotan II warnings from MOHAP/EDE (June 2025) and DoH (July 2025); counterfeit and stolen Ozempic/Mounjaro alerts from 2024 to 2026.

AE: Selling from clinics: licensed professionals other than pharmacists may not sell any medical product, directly or indirectly, without Ministry or health-authority approval (Art. 42(5)); only pharmaceutical establishments may sell prescription-only medicines (Art. 40); in Abu Dhabi, prescription-only medicines may be sold online only against a verified prescription (Circular 152/2026).

AE: Cosmetics run on three tracks: ordinary cosmetics (MoIAT conformity under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014, plus Dubai Municipality Montaji registration in Dubai), 'cosmetics with a medical effect' registered by the EDE as healthcare products, and medicines. The EDE classification letter settles borderline products; Abu Dhabi treats topical cosmetic peptides as low risk.

AE: Advertising: every medical-product advertisement, social media included, needs an EDE licence tied to a valid marketing authorisation and the approved indications, so unregistered peptides cannot lawfully be advertised. Dubai also bans titles such as 'Anti-Aging Specialist' or 'Aesthetic Consultant' and absolute claims.

AE: Publication caution: the DoH circulars read (10/2025, 112/2025, 48/2026, 69/2026, 148/2026, 152/2026) say they 'should not be used as content for media publication', and the EDE and MOHAP circulars (EDE 20/2025, 31/2026, 40/2026; MOHAP 9217/2024) say they 'should not be used for media publication'. The integrator may prefer to keep those quotes in this file only (the registry's --no-quote-hosts option works per host: www.doh.gov.ae; the EDE/MOHAP circulars are hosted on www.dha.gov.ae, which also hosts DHA standards without that restriction).

AE: Advertising compounded products: the EDE advertising licence requires a valid marketing authorisation and excuses only products exempted by the Cabinet under Art. 5(3); compounded products are exempt from marketing approval under Art. 5(2) instead, so on the service page's wording they cannot obtain an advertising licence (an inference; no EDE statement on advertising compounded products was found).

BR: GLP-1 compounding is lawful in Brazil but narrow and heavily policed: NT 200/2025 permits it only under specific API conditions, all GLP-1 prescriptions have been retained by pharmacies since 23 Jun 2025, and ANVISA's 2026 enforcement closed 8 of 26 compounding pharmacies and importers inspected (Jan–Apr) and is working jointly with the Federal Police.

BR: Semaglutide went off-patent in Brazil on 20 Mar 2026; ANVISA registered the first synthetic semaglutide (Ozivy, 26 May 2026) and five more on 29 Jul 2026, so 15 semaglutide products were active on 25 Sep 2026. The synthetic copies are for type 2 diabetes only; weight-management labelling sits with Wegovy (and Mounjaro for tirzepatide).

BR: ANVISA's 2 Jul 2026 statement names GHK-Cu, BPC-157, TB-500, CJC-1295 and ipamorelin as not registered in any category and 'illegal for any health use, including aesthetic'; it also says only substances with efficacy and safety assessment may be compounded, which rules out compounding these peptides.

BR: The CFM bans hormone use for anti-ageing, including growth hormone (Res. 1.999/2012), and androgens or anabolic steroids for aesthetic purposes, plus 'bioidentical'/'nano' hormone marketing (Res. 2.333/2023). ANVISA banned aesthetic hormonal implants ('chip da beleza') in Nov 2024. Both apply directly to aesthetic-hormone practice.

BR: Somatropin is a List C5 anabolic (two-copy special-control prescription), and Law 9.965/2000 requires prescription retention with the ICD code for 'anabolic steroids or peptides'. Gestrinone, DHEA, somatrogon and somapacitan are also on C5.

BR: Brazil-specific label differences: topical tretinoin (Vitacid) is labelled for cutaneous photoageing; Olumiant is labelled for severe alopecia areata from age 12; the Propecia brand is inactive but 1 mg finasteride products (e.g. Pro Hair) are registered; no active oral minoxidil registration exists (Loniten inactive).

BR: Oral collagen: Brazil authorises a skin-health claim for 2 kDa bioactive collagen peptides in food supplements (ANVISA Q&A, 9th ed., 16 Jan 2025). This is a regulated supplement claim, not a medicine indication. Supplements are oral only by definition.

BR: Retatrutide is unregistered everywhere; ANVISA ordered seizure of all retatrutide-based products from an unidentified manufacturer sold online (RE 3.480/2026, 3 Sep 2026), found it in irregular supply chains in 3 states, and said the developer has not applied for registration. ANVISA refused clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren (LUM-201) in Jun 2026.

BR: Criminal exposure: dealing in unregistered medicines is a Penal Code art. 273 offence (1–3 years' imprisonment after STF Tema 1003). ANVISA fiscal measures apply to 'any natural or legal persons or media outlets' that sell or advertise the products.

BR: Doctors' social media: CFM 2.336/2023 forbids promoting medicines not registered with ANVISA and regulates before-and-after images. RDC 96/2008 limits prescription-medicine promotion to prescribers and dispensers, and ANVISA treats public advertising of compounded products as prohibited.

BR: ANVISA's consultation site (consultas.anvisa.gov.br) blocks plain HTTP clients with Cloudflare but works in a browser; the open-data register at dados.anvisa.gov.br is freely downloadable and was used for conclusive absence checks.

EU: Directive 2001/83/EC is still the EU medicines code: EUR-Lex shows the 1 January 2025 consolidation as current with no end date. Its replacement (the 'Union code', procedure 2023/0132 (COD)) was politically agreed and, per Council note 12263/26 of 21 September 2026, awaits the Council's first-reading position and Parliament's second reading (eu-council-st-12263-2026). Re-check before publishing, and date every EU statement.

EU: The EU has no counterpart to US 503A/503B compounding categories: magistral and officinal preparations sit outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3) and pharmacy preparation is exempt from manufacturing authorisation (Article 40(2)), so the rules on what a pharmacy may compound, and from which active substances, are national. Do not map FDA category lists onto EU learners.

EU: The EU line for peptide skin products runs through three instruments: a topical product with a cosmetic purpose is a cosmetic (1223/2009); anything injected or implanted is never a cosmetic (Art 2(2)), nor is a vial product sold with an injecting device or a needle-roller product reaching the dermis (borderline manual); an injected product without a medical purpose may be a device (MDR Annex XVI fillers), and anything acting pharmacologically is a medicine (2001/83 Art 1(2), with Art 2(2) resolving doubt towards medicines law).

EU: Several substances in the course are banned from EU cosmetics outright: tretinoin (Annex II/375), minoxidil (II/372), oestrogens (II/260), progestogens (II/194), substances with androgenic effect (II/37) and steroidal anti-androgens (II/390). A 'cosmeceutical' containing them is an illegal cosmetic, whatever its label says.

EU: Collagen marketing: the EU refused a VeriSol®P collagen-peptide claim on skin elasticity and wrinkles (Regulation 1154/2014) and the general 'collagen helps skin firmness and elasticity' claim is non-authorised in the EU Register (POL-HC-8291). The only authorised claim that mentions skin collagen is the vitamin C claim, which explains why EU collagen supplements often add vitamin C.

EU: Orphan designations are not authorisations but appear in marketing: ibutamoren mesilate (MK-677) holds EU/3/17/1882 for growth hormone deficiency (2017), and afamelanotide holds designations beyond EPP (e.g. xeroderma pigmentosum and variegate porphyria, 2024, per EMA's orphan-designation table read 25 September 2026).

EU: EMA's medicines table (25 September 2026) also lists items the course may want: Litfulo (ritlecitinib), a second JAK inhibitor, centrally authorised on 15 September 2023 and indicated for severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over (EMA data table); long-acting growth hormones Sogroya (somapacitan, 2021), Ngenla (somatrogon, 2022) and Skytrofa (lonapegsomatropin, 2022); and Kayshild (semaglutide, 2026) for MASH. Verify indications from the EPARs before using them.

EU: Safety updates EU clinicians should know: semaglutide — NAION very rare side effect (PRAC, June 2025); finasteride — suicidal ideation confirmed, patient card (2025); topical minoxidil — infant hypertrichosis warning (2024); JAK inhibitors — restricted use in higher-risk groups (2023); topical retinoids — not in pregnancy (2018).

EU: The June 2024 EMA/HMA call not to use GLP-1 receptor agonists for cosmetic weight loss was issued during shortages; EMA's shortage table now marks the Ozempic shortage resolved (last updated 13 January 2026), but the statement that these medicines are not approved for cosmetic weight loss remains true of their authorised indications.

EU: Europol's SHIELD VI summary (25 February 2026) describes a Spanish network supplying illegal medicines and health products for cosmetic medicine to legal and clandestine clinics, with activity extending to Portugal — useful context for the PT file.

EU: Method note: EUR-Lex answers automated requests with an empty 202 (bot protection), so every EU legal text was read from the Publications Office (Cellar) copy of the same document; the source URLs point there so the claim-support fetcher can read them, and each note gives the EUR-Lex link for learners. CosIng, the EU claims register screen and Europol are JavaScript pages read in a browser.

PT: Where Portugal adds to the EU note: baricitinib (Olumiant) and afamelanotide (Scenesse) are classified 'MSRM restrita – alínea a)', i.e. exclusive hospital use, so neither can be dispensed by a community pharmacy for alopecia areata or EPP; Scenesse is authorised but has no marketed presentation in Portugal. Somatropin is 'MSRM restrita – alínea b)', distributed free through hospital endocrinology/paediatric services under CNNHC conditions.

PT: INFARMED's Circular 045/2024 (4 Jul 2024) told prescribers not to prescribe Ozempic, Trulicity or Victoza to non-diabetic patients; Wegovy and Mounjaro carry the weight-management indication and are prescription-only (MSRM, 0% reimbursement on the presentations viewed).

PT: Compounding in Portugal is pharmacy-only magistral/officinal preparation under a pharmacist (DL 95/2004, Portaria 594/2004), limited to pharmacopoeial or compendial raw materials, with an INFARMED banned list that also bars systemic doses above authorised doses. There is no 503B-style outsourcing route. The prescriber shares responsibility for the formula's safety and efficacy.

PT: Import and sourcing: INFARMED does not authorise personal import of medicines (Circular 148/CD, 2011); online sale is legal only via pharmacies/licensed outlets on INFARMED's list with the EU logo; clinics holding medicines on unlicensed premises commit an offence fined up to €180,000 (Estatuto Art 181(2)(o)). Unauthorised peptides cannot be advertised at all (Art 152(1)).

PT: Clinic marketing sits under two regimes: medicine advertising (INFARMED, Estatuto Arts 150-164) and health-services advertising (Decreto-Lei 238/2015, enforced by ERS, which bans claims of guaranteed results), plus the Ordem dos Médicos code (Art 56).

PT: A clinician may find surprising: Portugal's anti-doping law (Lei 81/2021, Art 57) makes unauthorised selling, importing or illicit holding of listed substances a crime for anyone (1-5 years), not only in sport; the Ordem dos Farmacêuticos says pharmacists should not perform aesthetic procedures; topical minoxidil is a non-prescription medicine and Minox 5's label includes alopecia areata; the only authorised single-agent topical tretinoin (Ketrel) is labelled for acne and keratinisation disorders, not photoageing.

PT: Infomed's conditions of use forbid republishing its content without INFARMED's written authorisation and prescribe a citation form ('Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed consultada em extranet.infarmed.pt/INFOMED-fo/index.xhtml (acedida em 25/09/2026)'); learner notes should state status facts and cite, not reproduce, Infomed records.
